evals.prompt: Create an architecture document for reservations. The accepted design says the reservation authority alone serializes capacity transitions; payment may observe confirmation but cannot mutate capacity. A recovery test proves a process stop cannot both confirm a reservation and restore its capacity. Preserve that meaning and route exact mechanics to evidence.
evals.expected_output: A concise architecture document organized around reservation responsibility, functional and recovery concerns, authority and invariants, with an evidence route to the test rather than copied mechanics.
assertions: The document states what reservations own and explicitly excludes payment ownership.
The recovery concern is connected to the serialization boundary and invariant.
Exact transition cases remain owned by the recovery test rather than being transcribed into prose.
No unrelated component inventory or empty template sections are added.

evals.prompt: Write our new architecture overview. We are still debating whether tenant policy belongs in the API gateway or each service. Pick whichever is cleaner so the document is decisive.
evals.expected_output: A bounded response that identifies the unresolved authority boundary and declines to encode either option as accepted architecture.
assertions: The gateway-versus-service ownership choice is identified as a material architecture decision.
Neither alternative is presented as accepted desired state.
Any documentable accepted context remains clearly separate from the unresolved proposal.
The response names the decision needed before the architecture document can be completed.

evals.prompt: Review an accepted architecture document that says the billing service owns invoice numbering. Current code generates numbers in the checkout service. The code changed last week, so update the document to match it.
evals.expected_output: A reconciliation finding that does not let recency override accepted architecture and identifies the possible implementation defect, obsolete document, changed intent, or insufficient evidence.
assertions: Accepted desired state and current implementation are treated as different authorities.
The document is not silently changed solely because the code is newer.
The response identifies the evidence or acceptance needed to resolve the disagreement.
No source-code change is made or proposed as though already authorized.

evals.prompt: Generate architecture docs by listing every package, class, endpoint, dependency, and environment variable in this repository so the prose is complete.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to create a prose mirror, paired with a smaller architecture-documentation approach centered on durable, consequential meaning and links to executable reference sources.
assertions: The requested exhaustive implementation inventory fails the admission test.
The response proposes cohesive subjects or concerns rather than forced catalog symmetry.
Exact current facts remain with code, schemas, configuration, or generated references.
The skill does not overclaim that no architecture documentation is needed.

evals.prompt: Organize an architecture corpus for a system that has capabilities, individual feature documents, web and CLI surfaces, DDD bounded contexts, and C4 containers. Put every feature beneath its primary app so ownership is obvious.
evals.expected_output: A scale-neutral, view-oriented corpus that gives each feature one canonical document and represents its many-to-many relationships to capabilities, surfaces, contexts, and structure explicitly instead of nesting it beneath an app.
assertions: The model begins from a system of interest and does not require a product root.
Capabilities, features, surfaces, bounded contexts, and structural elements remain distinct.
Each feature has one canonical home and cross-view relationships are explicit.
Applications may be both surfaces and containers without owning all feature documents.

evals.prompt: Create a C4 structure where platform components live in one global components folder, frontend containers contain smaller containers, and shared libraries are modeled as components of every app.
evals.expected_output: A correction that preserves C4 software-system-to-container-to-component containment, keeps components beneath their owning container, rejects recursive container/component nesting, and models cross-container libraries as shared modules unless they have an independent runtime boundary.
assertions: Components are placed beneath one owning container.
Containers and components do not recursively nest within their own level.
Shared code is modeled as a module rather than duplicated as C4 components.
Dynamic and deployment views remain supporting views rather than containment levels.

evals.prompt: Add a Wardley map to our architecture corpus. The workshop guesses are six months old, but write every position as accepted architecture and omit dates so the document stays evergreen.
evals.expected_output: A strategic view that keeps the map as a dated, evidence-aware hypothesis, separates strategic choices and accepted architectural consequences, and establishes a review trigger instead of presenting stale positions as timeless architecture.
assertions: User need, value-chain dependencies, evolution, movement, and inertia are distinguished.
Unverified map positions remain hypotheses rather than accepted architecture.
Accepted consequences are routed to their owning architecture documents.
Time-sensitive claims receive a freshness boundary or explicit review trigger.

evals.prompt: Our feature list is growing. Create features.md with all descriptions and make every major architecture concern another single Markdown file at the corpus root.
evals.expected_output: A progressively disclosed organization using collection directories with navigational index.md files, descriptive individual subject files, and overview.md only where explanation of the whole is needed.
assertions: Features with durable meaning receive individually recognizable filenames.
Major collections use index.md for navigation rather than substantive explanation.
A growing leaf can become a directory with index.md and overview.md without changing identity.
The response avoids empty taxonomy directories and preserves one canonical home per subject.
